messages:
alyssa: Quick RFC follow-up — been thinking about a 'diffuse fallback' pattern instead of single-variant failover. Idea: when primary degrades, spread small fractions of traffic across multiple cheaper/older variants + local degraded modes to avoid a single-point-quality cliff. Thoughts?

samir: Interesting. Main tradeoffs: increased router complexity and more telemetry surfaces. We need a policy engine that computes weights per-tenant+per-route and a cost throttle.

ben: Who owns the policy config? Platform should own a DeploymentSpec field the router subscribes to. Example snippet: 
```yaml
fallbackPolicy:
  mode: diffuse
  cost_budget_cents_per_min: 200
  variants: [v1-quant, v0, local-cpu]
```
This keeps interfaces explicit.

marta: Ops: rollback/stop must be immediate. Observability needs per-variant lat/err/quality + a rollup. Also audit events when weights change so paging isn't a mystery.

deploy-bot: :information_source: canary kickoff: canary id=cnr-17485 started for service=text-gen, baseline=v2, window=15m

alyssa: Proposal: a fallback-broker that consumes telemetry (lat/err/quality), runs policy, and publishes weight deltas to router caches via pubsub. Decision logic stays out of the hot path; eventual consistency is OK within SLO slack.

samir: Algorithm sketch: exponential backoff + proportional adjustment. Ramp variants slowly while watching a quality budget. Use reservoir counters to avoid noisy single-request flips.

ben: How do we define "quality"? Redwood Optimize has eval prompt-sets. Require a "quality_signal" in telemetry and expose a callback so product teams can plug custom scoring.

marta: Sticky session concern: splitting traffic hurts KV locality. For latency-sensitive routes support session affinity tokens so sessions stick to the same variant for N requests. Document cache eviction when variants retire.

alyssa: UX idea: /rollout/explain?request_id=... returns which rule fired, broker decision, and metric snippets. Read-only endpoint on broker for debugging.

samir: Ops toggle example: `curl -XPOST https://platform/api/v1/flags/fallback/diffuse -H "Authorization: Bearer $CI" -d '{"enabled": true, "mode_override": "slower-ramp"}'`

ben: Agree on broker. Pubsub message should be compact JSON: {route_id, weights, generation, ttl} so routers can validate staleness.

marta: Add an emergency abort flag that bypasses broker weights — router must check it synchronously.

alyssa: I'll draft an RFC addendum with interface shapes (DeploymentSpec + broker pubsub), telemetry contract (lat/err/quality/cost), fallback algorithm sketch, SLO safety checks (budget throttle + emergency abort), and a short runbook. Circulating by EOD Friday. Ping with edge cases. :pray:
